title: Evaluating 0/0 by Factoring a Difference of Squares
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

steps.title: Identify the Indeterminate Form
steps.explanation: Direct substitution yields 0/0, indicating the presence of a common factor (x - 3).
steps.why: The form 0/0 proves that x = 3 is a root of both numerator and denominator.

steps.title: Factor the Numerator
steps.explanation: Factor the difference of squares x^2 - 9 into (x - 3)(x + 3).
steps.why: Standard algebraic factorization identity a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b).

steps.title: Cancel Common Factor and Evaluate
steps.explanation: Cancel (x - 3) since x approaches 3 but x != 3, then substitute x = 3.
steps.why: If two functions agree everywhere except at x = c, their limits as x -> c are identical.
